rationale: Create one active Saragon platform record for the ten-site U.S. edge-colocation portfolio acquired from Cogent Fiber. The filed purchase agreement identifies ISQ Citadel Aggregator, L.P. as buyer and ties it to I Squared's Fund IV family; Cogent's June 29, 2026 Form 8-K confirms the $225 million closing, and I Squared launched the Saragon brand on August 19. The ten facilities are subordinate assets, not separate PortCos.

afterImage.description: Saragon is an I Squared Capital digital-infrastructure platform providing power-dense colocation capacity for AI inference, edge computing and interconnection workloads. The platform comprises ten fee-simple data-center properties across nine U.S. markets, with approximately 53 MW of capacity and 259,000 square feet. Its facilities are located in Atlanta, Baltimore, the Los Angeles area, Chicago, Houston, Kansas City, Nashville, Phoenix and Stockton. Cogent Fiber signed the sale agreement with ISQ Citadel Aggregator, L.P. on May 22, 2026, announced it on May 26 and completed the $225 million sale on June 29. I Squared launched the Saragon brand on August 19 and disclosed up to $1 billion of capital for the platform. The acquisition is attributable to the ISQ Global Infrastructure Fund IV family; the precise parallel fund, legal titleholders for individual sites and manager-level equity percentage are not publicly disclosed. Saragon is counted once as the manager-level platform, while its ten facilities remain subordinate assets. No subsequent sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.
